question: The perimeter of a rhombus is 148 cm and one of its diagonals is 70 cm. The area (in cm²) of the rhombus is:
solution:
**Given:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2e01fc11e1054c2f89aa21977c7759c3647d19b990681c949446b062c27a2582.png] 

The perimeter of a rhombus = 148 cm 

One of its diagonals = 70 cm

Concept used:

The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at 90°.

**Formula used:**

The area of the rhombus = (1 / 2) × Multiplication of the two diagonals

**Calculation:**

The side of the rhombus = 148 / 4 = 37 cm

Half of the other diagonal,

⇒ sqrt {(37)² - (35)²} 

⇒ sqrt{(37 + 35) (37 - 35)} 

⇒ sqrt{(72 × 2)} = √ 144 = 12 cm

Other diagonal = 2 × 12 = 24 cm

So, area = 1/2 (70 × 24) = 840 cm². 

**∴ The area of the rhombus is 840 cm2**
